entries.title: I Kings 14:1
segments: Parents are often punished in the sickness of their children, and should be led by it to repentance of their sins, and hearty consecration of themselves to the service and glory of God.

entries.title: I Kings 14:2
segments: Men who profess to believe that God is acquainted with all things, often act as if they hoped to deceive him; but all such efforts are vain, and will end in disappointment and sorrow.

entries.title: I Kings 14:3
segments:
Cracknels; a kind of cakes. 
 
Men are frequently more anxious to know the secret purposes of God, than to know his will for the sake of doing it.

entries.title: I Kings 14:5
segments: Though age and infirmities may lessen or destroy the human senses, God can, and if men are disposed to obey him, he will, reveal to them all they need to know in order to understand and do their duty.

entries.title: I Kings 14:7
segments: A man's guilt is aggravated in proportion to the blessings he has abused; and in the same proportion, unless he repent, will be his punishment.

entries.title: I Kings 14:8
segments:
Followed me with all his heart; not that he did not commit great transgressions, but he repented of them, and was sincerely devoted to the service of God. 
 
In reading the Bible, we are often called to witness that many things which take place in the course of providence and are accomplished by human instrumentality, are spoken of as done by God.

entries.title: I Kings 14:9
segments: Cast me behind thy back; treated him as unworthy of regard.

entries.title: I Kings 14:10
segments: By obedience to God, parents may be the means of bringing on their children great blessings, and by disobedience, great evils.

entries.title: I Kings 14:13
segments: Come to the grave; be buried with respect.

entries.title: I Kings 14:14
segments: Even now; what he predicted was certain and near.

entries.title: I Kings 14:15
segments:
As a reed is shaken; they would be subject to perpetual commotions. 
 
  Beyond the river; the river Euphrates.

entries.title: I Kings 14:17
segments: Tirzah; where Jeroboam lived, supposed to have been near Sechem.

entries.title: I Kings 14:21
segments: To put his name there; as the place where he would be publicly inquired of and worshipped.

entries.title: I Kings 14:22
segments: The course of human nature left to itself is downward from bad to worse, and the most highly exalted by privileges and blessings, when not restrained by divine grace, will become the most wretched and debased by their crimes.
